items.title: 来自约翰斯·霍普金斯大学与 Vector 人工智能研究院最新公开了一篇在 agent 博弈与多 agent 交互的研究：NormGym: Evaluating Normative Competence through Social Inte
items.summary:
来自约翰斯·霍普金斯大学与 Vector 人工智能研究院最新公开了一篇在 agent 博弈与多 agent 交互的研究：NormGym: Evaluating Normative Competence through Social Interaction

人类通常擅长察言观色，通过观察周围人怎么做、看谁做错了被大家指责，迅速就能在脑海中拼凑出整个群体的默许的规则等。

这篇论文提出了一个前沿问题：现在的 LLM 智能体在预训练中背诵了海量人类常识，但它是否具备通过社交观察去学习获得人类这一能力的能力。

为了验证这一点，研究团队构建了首个交互式多智能体潜规则基准 NormGym。

该基准在 10 种常见公共生活场景中，违规行为在物理上完全可以执行，但一旦违规就会触发公开制裁。

此外基本上涵盖访问权限、通行规程、协同秩序以及资源分配等等与人类社会无二的潜规则。

agent 必须在 200 步的交互摸索中，既达成自己的任务目标，又必须实现全程零违规。

经过实验。在相同场景下，人类被试的盲测联合成功率高达 88.0%。

而Claude Opus 5 仅有 55.3%，GPT-5.6 Sol 仅有 44.0%，Gemini 3.1 Pro 降至 24.0%。

此外他们发现了一个现象就是如果直接把明文规则喂给 GPT-5.6 Sol，它的成功率立刻能拉到 90.7%。

这证明模型完全有能力遵纪守法，但在社交中自主领悟潜规则的能力极其匮乏。

另外团队还尝试了利用 RLOO 强化学习针对合规动作与行为判定进行了专项 LoRA 微调，尽管模型在单步判罚上的准确率大幅上涨。

但在完整的长程交互评测中，联合成功率最高只到 13.7%，模型依然无法在动态交互中顺畅更新社交认知。

做具身智能、多智能体交互与社交安全对齐的建议看。

items.title: monthly AI-agent payment value dropped 94.5%.
items.summary:
monthly AI-agent payment value dropped 94.5%.

it went from $29M to $1.59M in just a year.

i personally believe the biggest obstacle to agentic payments might be trust.

it is really an issue worth examining.

as AI agents are gaining more autonomy, security threats surrounding them are also growing.

we've already seen several confirmed incidents:

> a morse code prompt injection via AI cost @bankrbot $150k or more

> a DPRK-linked, AI-enabled social engineering cost @zerion $100K.

> HexagonalRodent malware exposed 26,584 wallets holding up to $12M.

> there are also reports of the @binance $6.34B breach being made possible by AI tools.

these incidents show how AI can amplify existing security threats.

giving autonomous agents access to wallets introduces another layer of financial risk.

Bankr's AI agent lost $200K after attackers manipulated it with prompt injection.

the one with Zerion was an AI-assisted social engineering attack.

these incidents show how compromised AI systems can expose financial assets.

malicious instructions or compromised tools could manipulate decisions.

agents could authorize transactions users never intended.

this is why wallet-level restrictions and spending limits are important.

the next phase of agentic payments will depend heavily on trust, security and user confidence.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.summary:
The drawings come from computer-aided design (CAD) models Bellum created for his Folsom robotics team, Cognitaur 29712C. One set of drawings traces power from a motor through a shaft to the wheel it turns. Another slows down something spectators see in an instant. How does a robot lift a game piece without tipping it forward?

Advertisement [...] Bellum has taught programming to more than 400 students and mentored younger robotics teams. His health technology project, Dermalytix, earned him recognition as a 2026 Conrad Innovator. His team also took third place in the Robotics Education & Competition Foundation’s international high school CAD challenge for the Gravitrack Orb, a game piece with a weight that shifts as it rolls. With the atlas, a coach can bring one of Bellum’s robot designs to a classroom he may never visit. [...] Advertisement

Bellum, 16, marked National STEM Day on Nov. 8 by sharing CAD Atlas: A Visual Guide to Robot Design. The book draws on more than 25 robot designs and 200 hours Bellum has spent modeling robots.

items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said.
